articleTitle: Reducing HTML cache footprint through tracking data optimization: Insights from eBay
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Background Study: Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) caching [1] is a practice used in software systems to serve data quicker to incoming Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) requests [2]. Systems may cache rendered HTML or pre-rendered HTML either within the system or on the edge servers. Modern HTML renderer systems like React [3] and Marko [4] incorporate heuristics in the form of comments and attributes within the rendered HTML to facilitate efficient render and re-render processes.Problem Statement: In addition to these heuristics from rendering systems, the associated tracking systems embed additional data payload into HTML for end-user behavior tracking [5] These data payloads are crucial for internal tracking systems to assess the effectiveness of user features, based on the user behavior. However, these tracking data heuristics significantly increase the size of the HTML, posing challenges in scenarios where caching of the said HTML is required. The bulkiness of tracking data heuristics compared to rendering heuristics leads to inefficiencies in HTML caching.Proposed Model/Technique: This paper proposes an optimization technique that is focused on minimizing the size of the tracking data heuristics embedded in HTML. The technique aims to balance the need for effective user tracking with the efficiency of HTML caching. The novelty of the approach is that, it does not do pre-processing or post-processing of the embedded tracking heuristics but performs the said optimization alongside the render of the HTML, during the computation of the hydration [6] data. The approach involves a case study of eBay’s systems, where we explore methods to refine the data payloads without compromising the tracking capabilities.Results: The implementation of the proposed optimization technique in eBay’s systems demonstrated a significant reduction in cached HTML sizes, both in edge caching [7] and on the application servers. The optimized tracking heuristics maintained their efficacy in tracking user interactions and user behavior for specific product features, therefore showcasing the potential of this methodology to enhance caching efficiency without losing critical tracking functionalities and capabilities.

articleTitle: Contrastive Learning Hypergraph Neural Network Based on Multimodality Replacing Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Recommender systems are information filtering tools designed to recommend items of potential interest to users based on their preferences. Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based recommender systems have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance and introduced contrastive learning to improve robustness. However, as the number of GNN propagation layers increases, node features tend to become overly similar, making it difficult to capture user intentions and degrading recommendation performance. Furthermore, traditional data augmentation methods in contrastive learning exacerbate the data sparsity issue, making it problematic to generate high-quality item representations with limited interaction data. To address these challenges, we propose a Contrastive Learning Hypergraph Neural Network Based on Multimodality Replacing Data Augmentation (CHNM). The proposed method uses knowledge graphs to assist hypergraph structures in aggregating high-order information and capturing user-item relationships more precisely, thereby better identifying users' latent intentions. Additionally, multimodality replaces traditional data augmentation in contrastive learning, modeling the connection between multimodal features and items to optimize their representations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing methods across multiple benchmark datasets, validating the critical role of hypergraph structures and multimodality in enhancing recommendation performance.

articleTitle: Remaining useful life prediction for lithium-ion batteries based on multi-decomposition algorithm and CNN-BiLSTM-Attention
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: This study proposes a novel method for predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries, combining multiple decomposition algorithms (CEEMDAN and VMD) with a CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model. First, the battery capacity degradation sequence is decomposed into several intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). These IMFs are then categorized into high-frequency, medium-frequency, and low-frequency components using K-means clustering based on their complexity indicators. Subsequently, the high-frequency components undergo secondary decomposition to further refine their characteristics. Finally, the decomposed results are fed into the CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model for prediction. Validation using public lithium battery data provided by the Center for Advanced Life Cycle Engineering (CALCE) at the University of Maryland demonstrates that this method achieves the highest prediction accuracy, offering a new technical approach for lithium battery RUL prediction.

articleTitle: High-quality 3D generation method of ship targets based on multi-view diffusion model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: The 3D reconstruction of ship targets in shipping is very important for improving the ship's perception ability and autonomous navigation ability. However, the 3D reconstruction of ship targets in the shipping field is still a challenging task. This paper proposes a framework based on a multi-view diffusion model for the 3D reconstruction of ship targets. The framework uses a multi-view diffusion model and a multi-view reconstruction model to reconstruct the 3D model of the target ship from a single-view image, which can effectively extract the shape features and surface texture of the ship. The multi-view diffusion model generates multi-view images based on a stable diffusion model. The model is trained and adjusted using high-quality ship 3D data to improve the ability to generate multi-views. The results are provided to the multi-view reconstruction model to improve its reconstruction quality. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively realize the 3D reconstruction of marine ship targets in real time, and is superior to existing methods in terms of geometric shape, surface smoothness and texture quality. The proposed method significantly improves the 3D reconstruction quality of single-view ship images. By fine-tuning the multi-view diffusion model for generating ship scenes, the ability to generate multi-view ship images is improved. It has the ability to generate high-quality ship 3D models and can effectively improve the 3D perception ability of autonomous ships.

articleTitle: A Novel Dendritic Learning Approach for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have led to its extensive application in medical image processing, markedly enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of cancer detection. However, traditional models often struggle to effectively extract nonlinear features, which results in subpar performance when handling complex medical images. To overcome these challenges, we present a novel model architecture called Replicated Dendritic Visual Geometry Group (RepDVGG), designed specifically for the detection of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). RepDVGG leverages the depth advantages of the visual geometry group architecture of networks while incorporating a dendritic neural module (DNM) to enhance the processing of nonlinear features, thereby improving the feature learning capability of deep neural networks. Although the inclusion of DNMs adds complexity to the model, the structure of RepVGG facilitates efficient usage of structural re-parameterization during inference. Our experimental results on a publicly available NSCLC dataset reveal that RepDVGG outperforms several leading deep learning methods in both accuracy and computational efficiency. Specifically, in the NSCLC detection task, RepDVGG achieves a classification accuracy of 73.6% and an F1 score of 73.1%, surpassing traditional models such as GoogLeNet and ResNet. These findings indicate that the RepDVGG model, in conjunction with dendritic neural networks, offers significant advantages in the cancer detection domain and can serve as a valuable resource for clinical research.

articleTitle: HepatoAudit: A Comprehensive Dataset for Evaluating Consistency of Large Language Models in Hepatobiliary Case Record Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have shown significant potential in the medical field. However, most existing research focuses on general medical test sets, with relatively insufficient exploration in real clinical applications, especially in the field of complex diseases. To fill this gap, we introduce the HepatoAudit dataset – the first comprehensive dataset designed to evaluate the consistency of LLMs in generating diagnostic records for hepatobiliary diseases. This dataset is collected from the Chinese Clinical Cases Outcome Database and contains complete medical records that have undergone peer review, including patient basic information, chief complaints, history of present illness, personal history, family history, past medical history, physical examination, and laboratory tests. We have carefully selected 20 common hepatobiliary diseases, totaling 684 medical records. We systematically evaluated six mainstream large language models using four prompting methods. The experimental results show that although all models perform high in precision (with GPT-4 reaching a maximum of 93.42%), there are still significant deficiencies in recall, with the recall rate generally below 70%. In particular, for diseases with atypical symptoms or caused by multiple factors, such as splenomegaly, fatty liver, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes, the accuracy of the models is even below 40%.The main reasons are the insufficient understanding of the patient's complete medical history and symptoms by the large language models, as well as the lack of effective reflection and error correction mechanisms. Our research not only points out the challenges of LLMs in professional medical diagnostic tasks but also provides important directions for future improvements.

articleTitle: The Cognitive Diagnostic Model Incorporating Convolutional Neural Networks and Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Artificial intelligence is a key technology for smart education. The cognitive diagnostic model has been helpful in understanding the cognitive structure and learning state of students. In this paper, we take NeuralCD as a prototype, add the convolutional layer and introduce the attention mechanism. The Convolution Network and Attention Mechanism of Cognitive Diagnosis Model(CA-CDM) is constructed to predict student academic performance. The experiments show that the model's feature learning ability is enhanced, the information aggregation effect is also improved, the robustness is boosted, and the overfitting problem is also mitigated.

articleTitle: A Non-calibration-based Meter Reading Method for Substation Using Multi-Level Visual Model Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Existing methods for substation meter reading rely on manual calibration to obtain the meter's type, pointer position, and range information. Utilizing the prior information and neural network methods, meter values can be calculated. However, this approach relies on manual calibration data heavily, which limits its generalizability. Furthermore, the time-consuming manual calibration and configuration processes result in higher debugging expenses, which impends large-scale deployment. To overcome the challenge, this study proposes a non-calibration-based meter reading method using multi-level visual model aggregation, which is applicable to the complex environment of substations. First, a meter detection model is designed, spatial and channel attention mechanisms. This model is capable of extracting meter positions and identifying meter types from inspection images captured in substations. Subsequently, an instance segmentation model is adopted to extract meter range area information, which combines prototype mask generation and mask coefficient prediction to predict parallel sub-branches. Finally, a key point-based alignment correction model is proposed to solve the camera deviation caused by mechanical errors or environmental disturbances. It can achieve camera alignment correction and re-captures the target meter even under displacement scenarios of up to 30%. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been validated through practical applications in substations, demonstrating its robust performance in real-world scenarios.

Author Keywords: non-calibration-based meter reading meter detection model

articleTitle: Interpretable Automatic Rosacea Detection with Whitened Cosine Similarity
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: According to the National Rosacea Society, approximately 16 million Americans suffer from rosacea, a common skin condition that causes flushing or long-term redness on a person's face. To increase rosacea awareness and to better assist physicians to make diagnosis on this disease, we propose an interpretable automatic rosacea detection method based on whitened cosine similarity in this paper. The contributions of the proposed methods are three-fold. First, the proposed method can automatically distinguish patients suffering from rosacea from people who are clean of this disease with a significantly higher accuracy than other methods in unseen test data, including both classical deep learning and statistical methods. Second, the proposed method addresses the interpretability issue by measuring the similarity between the test sample and the means of two classes, namely the rosacea class versus the normal class, which allows both medical professionals and patients to understand and trust the results. And finally, the proposed methods will not only help increase awareness of rosacea in the general population, but will also help remind patients who suffer from this disease of possible early treatment, as rosacea is more treatable in its early stages. The code and data are available at https://github.com/chengyuyang-njit/ICCRD-2025. The code and data are available at https://github.com/chengyuyang-njit/ICCRD-2025.

articleTitle: Security and Credit evaluation mechanism federated learning privacy protection scheme
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Federated learning has been widely applied in fields such as government affairs, transportation, and healthcare due to its advantages in protecting the privacy of multiple parties while achieving secure modeling. It effectively solves the problem of information silos in the industry. This paper proposes a privacy protection scheme for federated learning based on homomorphic encryption and BLS signature technology, in response to the lack of gradient protection and the easy tampering of aggregation models in existing federated learning. In this paper, homomorphic encryption is used to protect the confidentiality of gradients uploaded by the client.; using BLS signature to protect the integrity of the aggregation model and prevent attackers from tampering with the aggregation model; the reputation evaluation algorithm can identify and reward participants who provide high-quality data and actively participate in the training process. Finally, Experimental evaluation shows that our approach significantly improves the protection of gradient and aggregation models in terms of security, while controlling performance loss within an acceptable range. Compared with existing solutions, our approach achieves better performance while ensuring high security.

articleTitle: An Automated Depression Diagnosis System Utilizing a Knowledge Base Created with GPT
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: We propose an automated depression diagnosis system using a knowledge base and GPT. This system detects depression from text posted on social media. This paper proposes an approach that utilizes knowledge graphs, which are a part of the knowledge base. In this research, we propose three models: a model with the knowledge graph of data from individuals with depression as input, a model with the knowledge graph of data from healthy individuals as input, and a model is supported to use knowledge graph from both depression individuals and healthy individuals. The proposed model achieved a precision of 89% and exceeded 90% in both recall and F1 score. The proposed method demonstrated the potential of using GPT as a system for detecting depression.

articleTitle: Specialized Accelerator for Arbitrary-Dimension Matrix Operations in Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: This paper addresses the significant challenge of executing inference tasks involving General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) in deep neural networks(DNN) on resource-constrained edge systems. While previous research has introduced various accelerator architectures for GEMM, these solutions primarily support matrix multiplications of varying dimensions at the software level rather than the hardware level. We propose an optimization of data reuse and memory access patterns through the integration of the outer product method. Building on this, we developed an optimized workload allocation strategy to further minimize data transfer overhead and balance computational resource utilization. Additionally, a heterogeneous hardware module named the Matrix Acceleration Engine (MAE) has been designed and integrated into the RISC-V processor to accelerate prevalent GEMM operations in deep neural networks. Compared to traditional instruction sets, the RV-MAE processor achieves a speedup of up to 194.74× in matrix operations and up to 20.29× in convolutional neural network tasks. Compared to advanced matrix accelerators, the performance is improved by 5.33×. Furthermore, the MAE, evaluated in a 28nm CMOS process, exhibits an area of 9742.18µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>and a power consumption of 2.9mW, thus meeting the low-power demands of edge computing.

articleTitle: Gangue Detection Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of yolo algorithm for coal gangue detection, a coal gangue detection model based on improved YOLOv5 is proposed. Construct datasets as close as possible to the real field environment. In this study, RReLU and Wise-IOU are used to replace the original loss function and activation function, and the backbone network is replaced with lightweight MobilNetV3. Target detection is carried out on the constructed gangue dataset, and the experimental results show that the improved algorithm improves the accuracy of the gangue detection by 5.7%, and the amount of computation decreases by 62.7%.

articleTitle: Analysis and Solution of Realtime Satellite Service Task Blocking Problem Caused by Resource Access Control Flaw
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: This paper delineates a real-time satellite task blocking problem stemming from flaws in the access control logic within the mutex semaphore acquisition function of an onboard real-time operating system. These flaws result in abnormal modification of mutex semaphore ownership, causing certain onboard real-time data processing task to abnormally halt execution. Through analysis of the system's real-time task scheduling mechanism and problematic data, the root cause of the problem is pinpointed, and a straightforward and effective resolution is proposed. Ultimately, the validation process and outcomes of this method are presented.

articleTitle: Group-SENet: A Lightweight Channel Attention Mechanism for Food Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: With the increasing severity of food waste, accurate food recognition technologies have gradually become an important tool for reducing food waste and optimizing food management. Although deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have made significant progress in various fields, including image recognition, the application of high-precision models in food recognition tasks faces significant challenges related to computational resources and real-time processing due to the limitations of IoT hardware. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lightweight channel attention module, Group-SENet, which enhances the inter-channel information interaction by grouping and reordering the input feature maps along the channel dimension. Furthermore, it combines channel attention with spatial attention mechanisms, enabling the network to capture both spatial and channel features while avoiding feature loss caused by compression operations, and thereby maintaining a low computational overhead.

articleTitle: Application of Natural Language Processing Algorithms for Chatbots
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant increase in published research on deploying various machine learning (ML) methods and algorithms in the development of chatbots for diverse applications. Substantial evidence indicates that top IT companies globally employ intelligent solutions to improve customer service and support. Typical chatbot implementation often involves rule-based systems, where each question is matched with a specific rule or predefined response. However, this principle is impractical for vast amounts of data, where users can always ask questions that are out of the scope of predefined rules. This paper demonstrates the implementation of NLP algorithms in chatbots, using machine learning and custom Python functions to improve user interaction by accurately answering domain-specific questions and providing appropriate feedback for questions outside its scope.

articleTitle: Cellular Automata as a Tool in Artificial Life Research
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Decentralized spatially extended systems, such as cellular automata (CA), have intrigued scientists since the pioneering work of John Von Neumann and others in the mid20th century, subsequently popularized by John Conway in the 1970s. This paper provides an overview of cellular automata and its evolution as a tool in artificial life (Alife) and complex systems research. The paper explores the origins of CA, from Von Neumann's early work on self-replicating automata to Conway's Game of Life and Stephen Wolfram's contributions. It also delves into the development of non-discrete aspects of CA, such as cyclic particle systems and multiple neighborhood cellular automata. By summarizing these developments, this paper contributes to our understanding of how CA has become a valuable instrument in the study of complex systems and artificial life.

articleTitle: Design of FIR Filter with Linear Group Delay in Passband Using Marine Predator Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: In FIR filter design, if the system only requires linear phase in passband or a certain frequency domain interval but nonlinear phase in other frequency domain intervals, the FIR filter design method with symmetric coefficients is no longer applicable. A design method for FIR filter with linear phase in passband using Marine Predator Algorithm is proposed. The optimization goal of this method is the minimum group delay error in passband, and the constraint conditions are the full frequency domain amplitude errors. Experimental results show that the FIR filter designed by this method has good amplitudefrequency characteristics and linear phase in passband. This method is simple to implement, has low computational complexity, and can be widely used in the field of digital signal processing.

articleTitle: Financial Sentimental Analysis for Argument Mining Using Prompt-Based Fine-Tuned LLaMA3
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: This study proposes an argument mining technique for automatically extracting logical relationships between paired sentences. The method aims to identify elements such as grounds and counterarguments within financial documents and to model their relationships, enabling a clearer understanding of the overall argumentative structure of the documents. To achieve this, we fine-tuned LLaMA3 using Prompt-Based Fine-Tuning, achieving a Micro-F1 Score of 84.5% and a Macro-F1 Score of 67.1%, which are higher than those reported in previous studies. This system is expected to simplify and improve the accuracy of financial document analysis conducted by investors during decision-making processes, thereby enhancing the practicality of utilizing financial information.

articleTitle: Development and Performance Analysis of Information Network Application Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: The era of network information is an era of explosive development of information networks. Starting from the perspective of network applications, this article combines the development status of network application models such as peer-to-peer (P2P) model, file server (FS) model, client/server (C/S) model, and browser/server (B/S) model, and systematically sorts out the basic connotation and technical characteristics of the current mainstream information network application models, Summarized and analyzed the application advantages, weaknesses, and applicable scenarios of typical network application models, and explored the development trend of application models for cloud structured information networks in the future, which has reference value for studying information network application models.

articleTitle: A Rigorous Approach to Specify System Behavior for Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: In this paper, we provide an attempt on specifying faulty behavior of autonomous systems, and the rigorous verification using formal methods. Faulty behaviors modeled in this method can enhance the capability to detect complex, time-related system faulty behaviors for fault diagnosis. Faulty behaviors modeled by temporal facts, which act as the bridge between diagnosis software and the formalized verification of the specification, can be interpreted in temporal logic formulas to capture the intended time-related system requirement. We use model checking technique to verify the correctness of the fault models expressed by temporal facts. Fault models are not specified in a formal form; therefore, the domain experts can focus on the issues in the business domain when they try to specify system faulty behaviors. In practice, we build a fault diagnosis system based on temporal facts, and employ model checking to automatically verify the intended behavior of system fault. The verifiable fault models provide the domain expert a rigorous and reliable approach to specify system behaviors.

articleTitle: Spectral Attention Feature Selection for Patient Mortality Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Patient representation learning for disease prediction is becoming increasingly important. EHRs as an crucial data source for patient representation learning. However, due to the large number of EHRs features, only some of them are relevant to disease prediction. Secondly, a large number of features will also bring redundant information, thereby reducing the accuracy of the model. To address this issue, we use the attention mechanism to learn the correlation of features in EHRs. We propose a spectral attention feature selection framework that not only reduces time overhead but also minimizes the impact of redundant features. We apply our method to existing healthcare models, and the experimental results verify the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Freshness Prediction Method for Large Yellow Croaker Based on Attention Mechanism Enhanced Time Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: During the process of spoilage, large yellow croaker produces gases such as CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S, NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, TMA, etc. TMA is a crucial metric for assessing how fresh fish is. Fish freshness can be predicted based on TMA content. Conventional detection techniques can harm fish and are complicated. Thus, using Internet of things technology and incorporating a neural network attention mechanism, this article suggests a freshness prediction approach for huge yellow croakers. Time series data is produced through the real-time monitoring of CO2, H2S, NH3, and TMA during the refrigerated yellow croaker spoiling process. In order to forecast the TMA value of the giant yellow croaker during the decay process, this study suggests a new prediction model called ATCN. When compared to conventional PLS models, the ATCN model has improved evaluation metrics by roughly 77.6% in MSE, 52.6% in RMSE, and 51.6% in MAE. The findings show that the model is capable of accurately predicting the huge yellow croaker's freshness.

articleTitle: Barriers to Developing M-Government Websites: Citizen Engagement, Security, and Data Privacy
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Mobile government (m-government) leverages mobile technology in enhancing government services while promoting citizen engagement and at the same time improving service delivery. Since mobile integration nowadays has been an integral part of almost everyone, government agencies can reach out to citizens more conveniently, efficiently, and timely and provide prompt service. However, those challenges must be considered and address to help in the successful development and implementation of m-government platforms. The scope of this research has a comprehensive literature review by using thematic analysis to identify the factors preventing from a successful m-government website development. It is mainly focusing on three thematic areas such as citizen engagement, security challenges and data protection issues on developing mobile government websites. Finding reveals that mobile government platforms have problems in terms of citizen engagement, security issues and privacy. Among these other factors that significantly act as a barrier to citizen engagement include accessibility, functionality problems, complex interfaces, inadequate digital literacies, lack of feedback mechanisms, poor mobile compatibility, lack user-experience and lack of trust in the government which may result from discouraging people from adopting mobile government services. Because user acceptance is a critical factor for successful mobile government solutions, it must be that taken into consideration when implementing mobile government programs effectively. Data privacy and security challenges includes data breaches, misuse of personal information, and the minimization of personal data collection and the possible cyberattack and threats due to exposure of data and weak security measures. Subsequent research should focus more broadly on inclusive design approaches, ensure robust security controls, privacy-by-design and transparent data management should be enforced in order to protect users and build trust for such services. In addition, the current research sets a base for future studies and reviews that will be conducted concerning the present challenges and opportunities related to the development of m-government sites, further encouraging technological and policy development.

articleTitle: Short time step prediction of moisture content of construction materials based on VAR modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to explore the feasibility and effectiveness of utilizing Vector Autoregression (VAR) model to predict the moisture content of construction materials. The moisture content of construction materials has an important impact on their performance, durability and safety. Reasonable control of moisture content can prolong the service life of materials, improve the quality and efficiency of construction, reduce energy consumption, lower economic costs, and improve environmental adaptability. However, traditional water content prediction methods mostly rely on empirical data and simple statistical models, which are difficult to accurately capture the complex relationship between multiple variables. For this reason, this paper proposes a prediction method based on the VAR model in order to overcome the limitations of the traditional methods. Experimental results show that the VAR model exhibits high accuracy in predicting the water content of construction materials, and its MAE, RMSE, and MAPE are better than those of the commonly used deep learning models such as CNN and LSTM. This may be attributed to the lower computational complexity of the VAR model and its effective capture of stable relationships.

articleTitle: Meta-weighted Prototype Contrastive Rehearsal for Online Continual Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Offline deep learning methods often suffer from catastrophic forgetting when applied to online learning scenarios. Online continual learning (CL) addresses this challenge by learning new knowledge from non-stationary data streams while retaining previously learned knowledge. However, in online CL, data imbalance gives rise to model bias towards the new classes and the impacts of different samples vary greatly across different learning stages. To address these issues, we propose a Meta-weighted Prototype Contrastive Rehearsal (MPCR) framework for online CL. MPCR dynamically assigns appropriate weights to each sample during training, effectively balancing their influence on model learning. Unlike traditional methods that depend on predefined priors, MPCR offers more flexibility and adaptability. Additionally, we provide a Least-Recently-Used (LRU) Buffer update strategy, which leverages the sampling time of examples to prevent overfitting on the buffer set. Extensive experimental results on three public online CL benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: FPGA-based Real-time High-resolution Image Processing for rocket on-board processing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: The structure of the rocket-borne model is inherently complex, with processed images exhibiting high resolution and generating substantial amounts of data and calculations. Achieving robust real-time computing on an embedded platform poses significant challenges due to strictly limited resources, power consumption constraints, and size limitations. Our review of rocket-borne applications reveals considerable variability in the design resources of different devices, indicating a need for expanded design approaches. Upon evaluating existing methods, we identified two primary drawbacks. First, certain operators within the high-resolution target detection model are difficult to parallelize, resulting in significant inference delays that hinder the ability to meet task requirements. Although existing methods have been extended, there remains significant potential for performance enhancement in core scheduling for poor acceleration. This paper proposes an optimized architecture for the target detection algorithm accelerator designed for high-resolution images, along with a novel highly parallel data pre-processing and post-processing module implemented on FPGA to address these issues. Compared to the ARM implementation, this architecture demonstrates an improved performance of 24.64x. Furthermore, to ensure flexible application across various rocket launch scenarios, we introduce an optimization structure for convolution, pooling, and fusion operators and a multi-core expansion optimization method. This approach yields a 1.29x improvement in computing unit utilization compared to state-of-the-art multi-core scaling efforts. Finally, we assessed the accelerator architecture across multiple FPGA platforms, achieving a peak processing element utilization rate of 99.71% for a single core and layer. The overall computing efficiency, excluding the first layer, exceeded 90%. The peak computing power for the four cores reached 1638.4 GOPS, and the end-to-end computation time for YOLOv5s with a 512×512 input was reduced to under 15 ms, making it suitable for aerospace applications that demand strong real-time performance and low power consumption.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Advanced RAG Techniques using Mahabharata
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a hot topic and one of the most compute-effective context-extending techniques in the LLM industry. Unfortunately, RAG also faces certain challenges, which make it vulnerable to mistakes. To overcome these challenges, recent studies have come up with numerous methods, which are collectively referred to as advanced RAG. In our study, we test out the effectiveness of individual Advanced RAG methods and compare them when used with a variety of LLMs. We perform this comparative study using the Mahabharata, the Indian Epic, as the external knowledge base. Examining how Advanced RAG techniques can be used in practical applications is this paper’s primary contribution. We then test the efficacy of the techniques using answer-independent evaluation metrics. We conclude by tabulating the performance metrics recorded and provide insights on the results obtained.

articleTitle: A Corpus-based Analysis of China’s Political Discourse
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Government image, by virtue of influencing public perception and trust, plays an important role for the attainment of sustainable governance for governments. Government work reports as a key form of political discourse, delineate the policy orientations and priorities of governments and encapsulate a wealth of political information and values. This empirical study, adopting Appraisal System and the evaluative adjectives within framework of Systemic Functional Grammar, analyzes the government image presented in the English version of China’s government work report, and explores what kind of governance is communicated to the national and international audiences. This corpus-based study reveals that through the linguistic resources of appreciation and modalization in general, and through ‘value’ and ‘degree’ evaluative adjectives in specific, the producers of Chinese political discourses skillfully employ evaluative vocabulary in exhibiting a government image that is accountable, effective, responsive, and inclusive, which are major attributes of good governance. This interdisciplinary study, therefore, deepens and enriches the scope of research on government image and governance from a corpus-based perspective.

articleTitle: KurtaGen: LoRA-Enhanced Diffusion for Indian Traditional Garment Design Generation and Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: The fast-paced growth of fast fashion and the convenience of buying clothes online have changed everything in the past few years. Technological advancements have enabled faster mass production of more fashionable designs than ever; however, it often comes in exchange for garment quality, personalization, and long-term customer satisfaction. Online shopping sites frequently fail to deliver on particular customer preferences, thus prompting many to rely on offline modes for more tailored options. Indian garments remain a timeless symbol of culture, tradition, and elegance with a lot of intricacies and details, often requiring extensive customization. Despite the substantial scope of technological advancement through digitizing the designing process of such garments, this realm of fashion remains unexplored in terms of technology. This paper introduces KurtaGen, a model based on Stable diffusion XL enhanced by the usage of Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA). This model is developed for designing Indian garments having great detail and variety, with a particular focus on Kurtas. This was achieved by training the diffusion model on our custom dataset, Kouture, whose in-depth annotations help bring special attention to detail in the garment designing process. Furthermore, this model also enables one to further realize their vision of the garment through prompt-based fashion image editing utilizing the diffusion model. Our model provides a step towards a more personalized digital future of fashion design, allowing users to realize specific garment visions through prompt-based image generation and editing.

articleTitle: Customer Purchase Intention Prediction Based on Stacking Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: The prediction of customer purchase intention represents a crucial aspect of business operations. Over recent years, there has been an increasing interest in business and academic communities in this field. Nevertheless, enterprise services continue to face some significant challenges. From a macro-level point of view, the existing methods only apply to an individual enterprise and its dataset rather than to multiple enterprises. Extracting meaningful features from a substantial quantity of raw data, enhancing prediction model accuracy represent significant requirements and challenges. In this work, we propose an adaptive stacking ensemble model for predicting customer purchase intention to address these challenges by improving model performance. We use real-world data from over 300 enterprises and propose the following methods. Firstly, we design an adaptive feature selection approach to automatically select the better feature combination. What's more, based on widely used supervised learning algorithms and stacking ensemble methods, we propose a stacking-fusion model to optimize the performance of prediction algorithms. The experimental results show that the proposed approach demonstrates notable enhancements in the F1-score across the three enterprises, with improvements ranging from 18.28% to 40.31% compared to the benchmark algorithm. The approach proposed in this paper exhibits a notable enhancement in performance and efficiency, offering a superior approach for customer purchase intention prediction.

articleTitle: Comparison of Vision Transformer with Convolutional Neural Networks for Brain Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Brain cancer is one of the most deadly illnesses. It causes abnormal cells to grow in the brain. Planning for treatment and the prognosis of patients with brain tumors depend greatly on early diagnosis. Brain tumors can have different characteristics, treatments, and forms. Consequently, the process of manually detecting brain tumors is difficult, labor-intensive, and error-prone. Doctors use magnetic resonance imaging to detect those abnormal cells in the brain. With the growth of artificial intelligence, it is possible to diagnose the brain tumor from MIR images. For instance, convolutional neural networks and transformers could be used. The self-attention mechanism is implemented by transformers, which are models that give each input data component a distinct weight. Transformers have limited applications in image classification tasks because they were originally designed for use in natural language processing applications. Thus far, the majority of image classification research has employed convolutional neural networks. In this paper, six different pretrained convolutional neural networks and a vision transformer are used to classify four distinct brain tumor classes. The models include ResNet50, AlexNet, VGG16, InceptionV3, MobileNetV2, FractalNet, and the Vision Transformer. The goal of this study is to compare the performance of these pretrained convolutional neural network models with that of the vision transformer, demonstrating that transformers can also be effectively applied to image classification tasks. The performance of a vision transformer model shows 84.39% accuracy in the classification problem, which is better than the other six architectures.

articleTitle: Genetic Crossover Operator with Staged Crossover Strategy for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: The Genetic Algorithm (GA) has been successfully applied to the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP), a classic NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem. The complexity of CVRP renders exact methods nearly infeasible, necessitating heuristic and metaheuristic approaches. GA is a widely used metaheuristic approach for obtaining near-optimal solutions, with the crossover operator playing a critical role in the algorithm’s optimization effectiveness and efficiency. Although the Sequential Constructive Crossover (SCX) is one of the most effective crossover operators, it has the drawback of easily getting trapped in local optima. Given the limited research on improvements to SCX, this paper addresses this gap by proposing a Staged Crossover Strategy that Staged Sequential Constructive Crossover (SSCX) from a new perspective. This strategy introduces new individuals to enhance diversity, aiming to overcome the limitations of SCX. Extensive experiments on VRP instances of varying scales demonstrate that the improved algorithm significantly enhances optimization performance for large-scale CVRP instances, achieving an average improvement of approximately 5-18%.

articleTitle: Research on a Personalized License Plate Recognition Algorithm Based on the LPRNet Model
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Automatic recognition of vehicle license plates has become a core issue in the construction and management of smart cities and intelligent transportation systems both domestically and internationally. Core recognition algorithms face significant challenges due to varying lighting conditions, diverse background colors, personalized license plates, and the visual similarity of characters. This paper proposes an improved recognition model based on the LPRNet model—SE-Bi-LPRNet. This model employs YOLOv8 for precise localization of the license plate area and introduces an attention layer that integrates attention and contextual mechanisms. By incorporating a bidirectional long-short-term gated algorithm and threshold selection, it effectively addresses complex background environments. The attention layer enhances the recognition accuracy of visually similar characters, while the bidirectional gating algorithm improves adaptability in complex scenes. Experimental results show that SE-Bi-LPRNet achieves a recognition accuracy of 96.79% in complex environments and 95.32% in personalized character recognition, significantly outperforming traditional LPRNet and other methods while maintaining competitive processing times. These improvements highlight the robustness and application potential of the model in intelligent transportation systems. Future research will explore integrating Transformer encoders into the model to enhance sequence modeling capabilities and overall performance.

articleTitle: An Automated Diagnosis of Diabetic Retinopathy Grading Using DenseNet169
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: This study used DenseNet121, DenseNet169, DenseNet201, EfficientNetB0, EfficientNetB7, Inception ResNetV2, Inception V3, MobileNet, MobileNetV2, MobileNetV3Large, ResNet50, ResNet101 and ResNet152, 13 different deep learning neural network models were used for automatic grading of diabetes retinopathy(DR). The change of Validation Accuracy trend was initially observed with 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50, different EPOCHs. Before grading, pre-processing such as elimination, amplification, denoising, data enhancement, normalization, etc. were carried out for the problems in the retinal image data set in the experiment. Then we used the deep learning neural network model proposed in this study to embed the attention mechanism into DenseNet169 for automatic grading of DR, enable deep learning neural network models to focus on features such as exudates, thick blood vessels and microaneurysms in retinal images. In order to avoid vanishing gradients in the neural network model and ensure classification accuracy, DenseNet169 was adjusted by using a targeted swish function for processing, and classify retinal images into three levels and finally the classification accuracy of the neural network model proposed in this study reached 99.76%, macro avg precision reached 99.76%, macro avg recall reached 99.76% and macro avg f1-score reached 99.76%. It is significantly better than other models and on average. It can correctly identify and automatically grading more than 4600 images in the verification of 4,617 retinal images. The method proposed in this study has been validated to effectively improve the accuracy of DR classification and can be used for large-scale DR medical imaging screening. It can effectively assist doctors in achieving efficient diagnosis of DR grading. This work was supported by Research Program of Qilu Institute of Technology (No.QIT24NN032).

articleTitle: The Application of Cross-modal Consistency Enhancement and Feature Fusion in High-frequency Feature-driven Face Forgery Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: With the rapid development of related technologies, face forgery techniques have become increasingly sophisticated. Meanwhile, it brings some potential risks. An improved dual-stream structural model is proposed in this paper which can effectively processes RGB features and high-frequency features for forgery detection. The model not only extracts multi-scale high-frequency features and performs cross-modality consistency enhancement (CMCE) at the input stream but also extracts residual-guided spatial features, providing rich information for subsequent feature fusion and classification. In the middle stream, multiple dual cross-modality attention (DCMA) modules are used to model the interaction between the two modality feature mappings, which strengthen the representation of relevant features by calculating the similarity between the two modalities. An attention-based feature fusion strategy (CAFMF) is introduced, which can more efficiently integrate the information of features from different levels. The experimental results show that the improved model, trained on the public dataset FaceForensics++, achieved AUC values of 98.81%, 98.17%, 98.94%, 94.39%, 65.75%, 80.90%, and 77.58% on DF, F2F, FS, NT, FaceShift, Celeb-DF v1,and Celeb-DF v2 respectively. The results demonstrate it get good performance in cross-dataset generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: Improving the RAG-based Personalized Discharge Care System by Introducing the Memory Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: As the performance of large language models is proven in general domains, we can consider applying them to specific tasks to improve the system’s specialization and responsiveness. In this paper, we will develop a lightweight software system based on RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) to test whether this approach can provide effective advice and protection for patients after discharge. All patient data in this study comes from the neurology department. We will select three diseases — Acute Cerebral Infarction, Atherosclerosis, and Hypertension to test our system, and the generated results will be evaluated by professional doctors. Additionally, we will introduce a memory mechanism to enhance the system’s performance and responsiveness. Finally, we will include suggestions for system improvements and extensions. The experimental results indicate that both the foundational capabilities of large language models (such as Llama 3 and GPT-4) and the system architecture (e.g., the integration of RAG and memory mechanisms) significantly influence overall performance. By comparing different models and architectures, it is observed that the GPT-4 system combined with RAG and memory mechanisms outperforms the baseline in terms of total score and improvements, demonstrating the effectiveness of system architecture optimization in enhancing the models’ ability to handle complex tasks. Since the data still contains sensitive information of patients and hospitals after being desensitized, we cannot show all the test data. However, after obtaining the hospital’s permission, through data desensitization, we showed some of the test data. You can click here to get the prototype we developed and some test data.

articleTitle: Sustaining Solar Panel Cleanliness with Multiclass Classification of Panel Images Using Deep Learning & ML Classifiers Trained on SVD Embeddings
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Maintaining the optimal performance of solar panels poses a complex challenge, especially in regions abundant in solar energy like deserts and tropical areas. This research paper explores the utilization of machine learning and deep learning techniques in categorizing the states of solar panels through visual image processing. In regions where solar farms are increasingly prevalent, challenges such as dust accumulation, cracks, and delamination hinder energy production and diminish solar panel efficiency. Our study employs various machine learning classifier models and deep learning to a unique dataset comprising real-world images of solar panels categorized into distinct groups: clean panels, dusty panels, and panels exhibiting breaks and delamination. The aim is to distinguish between surfaces that are clean, cleanable (dirty), and uncleanable (surface breakage and delamination).Given the high dimensionality of our novel image data (120000), we leverage dimensionality reduction with singular value decomposition (SVD) in our study to train the machine learning classifier models. An SVD dimensionality reduction approach shows excellent compression with a compressed 10-dimensional SVD embedding obtaining high accuracies and F1 scores when used to train our ten machine learning algorithms. We obtain a peak F1 score as well as a balanced accuracy of 0.96 with the trained support vector machine classifier (SVC) model using our ten-dimensional SVD embeddings as the input. Several decision tree-based models perform well too with a F1 score of 0.85 for an Adaboost classifier, 0.9 for an extra tree classifier, 0.93 for our decision tree classifier, and 0.94 for the bagging classifier model. We also create and train a custom deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) with 2566129 parameters on the uncompresses data that performs extremely well. We obtain a micro precision, recall, and F1-score of 0.98 as well as a macro precision of 0.99, macro recall of 0.98, and macro F1-score of 0.98 for our DCNN model. The weighted precision, recall, and F1-score are found to be 0.98. The output of these two approaches have been compared in terms of accuracy and time complexity. The Deep CNN performs better in terms of accuracy, but with a marginal decline in performance, the ML algorithms trained on the SVD embedding, especially SVC, Nu SVC and Bagging classifiers enable tremendous savings in terms of space and time complexity (by a factor of 14450) over the DCNN by order of magnitudes.

articleTitle: Gradient Descent Based Polarization Channel Estimation in Extremely Largescale MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Accurate channel model and channel estimation are crucial for achieving extremely large-scale multiple-inputmultiple-output (XL-MIMO) in 6G networks with ultra-high spectral efficiency. As the aperture of the antenna array increases dramatically in XL-MIMO scenarios, the electromagnetic propagation field will change from far-field to near-field. In this paper, we propose a gradient descent-based near-field XL-MIMO channel model (GD-SOMP), an algorithm that makes the discrete adoption points more continuous to improve the estimation accuracy to match the actual near-field XL-MIMO scenarios. Numerical simulation results show that the GD-SOMP algorithm outperforms the conventional near-field channel estimation algorithm in terms of mean square error performance.

articleTitle: Design and Research of AI Accelerators for Onboard Computing Platforms Targeting YOLOs Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) play a crucial role in computer vision, with wide applications in image recognition, object tracking, and trajectory optimization. Due to constraints in computation, power consumption, and size in aerospace vehicles, deploying CNN algorithms on target platforms presents a significant challenge in aerospace applications. This paper proposes an accelerator design for the YOLOv3-tiny network tailored to aerospace applications. By employing techniques such as loop partitioning, loop unrolling, and weight sharing, the proposed accelerator enhances computational performance and data reuse efficiency. Additionally, by integrating convolution, activation, and pooling operations into a unified module, this approach reduces the need for intermediate buffers, saving memory and improving acceleration performance. Compared to accelerators that require buffering of convolution results, the proposed design demonstrates superior performance. The accelerator is implemented on the ZYNQ7020 FPGA platform, achieving a peak computational performance of 114.53 GOPS.

articleTitle: Research on an Adaptive Chaotic Firefly Satellite Selection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: To address the issues of high computational complexity and susceptibility to local optima in traditional satellite selection algorithms for Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), this paper proposes an Adaptive Parameter Chaotic Firefly Algorithm (APCFA). The algorithm enhances global search capability and local convergence efficiency by introducing dynamic parameter adjustment and chaotic mapping, making it particularly suitable for complex nonlinear and multi-peak satellite selection problems. APCFA demonstrates significant advantages in balancing selection precision and computational efficiency, providing an efficient and reliable solution for satellite selection in GNSS.

articleTitle: Statistical Language Model for Information Retrieval System Implementation in Digital Library
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: A digital library is an application of technology to traditional libraries, providing access to various resources like books, magazines, and newspapers in digital formats. This allows users to access information anytime and anywhere with an internet connection. However, current digital library systems still face challenges, particularly in performing contextual searches for documents. Additionally, the order of search results does not always indicate how relevant the documents are to the user's query. This research explores the use of Statistical Language Models (SLM) to enhance the information retrieval system (IRS) process in digital library applications. SLM uses statistical techniques to analyze the semantic relationships between documents and users, increasing the efficiency and relevance of data collection. This research aims to identify the strengths and weaknesses of SLM, apply it to the IRS application, and evaluate its effectiveness for the application to be developed. These findings contribute to the development of an effective IRS, increasing the efficiency and accessibility of digital library applications and increasing the integration of SLM in IRS in the future.

articleTitle: Detailed Explanation of High-speed Transmission Parameter Index System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: In the process of implementing high-speed transmission requirements, contractors generally provide feedback indicating a lack of experience, making it difficult to understand the test content and effectively utilize test results, etc. This paper offers a detailed explanation of the high-speed transmission parameter index system, primarily discussing the following aspects: 1. The specific meaning of each parameter and the purpose of the tests; 2. The impact mechanism of each parameter on high-speed transmission performance and its changing patterns; 3. The testing principles and methods for each parameter; 4. Common reasons for these parameters being unqualified, and how to ensure their compliance through design and process; 5. The trade-offs and considerations in assessing these parameters during the design and production process.

articleTitle: Deep neural network interpretability for image classification based on semantic compressed perception
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning technology, as one of the core tasks in the field of computer vision, the accuracy of image classification has been significantly improved. However, as a black-box model, the decision process of deep neural network for image classification is hard to be intuitively understood and interpreted, which will lead to security risks in applications requiring high transparency and security. In this paper, we initially propose a deep neural network interpretability method for image classification based on semantic compressed perception, aiming to explore the learning and decision mechanism of deep learning models through complex network theory and semantic compressed theory. Compressed perception technology is applied to capture the semantic characteristics of image data. The local clustering coefficient and node centrality in complex network theory are utilized to find the representative sample image instance of each category in the training set, and such that we explore the interpretability of the model from a new perspective. This method is an interpretability method for the synthesis of concept-level features and image-level features, and it is speculated that a deep learning model for image classification may corresponds to an image semantic compressed method. The work in this paper not only helps to understand the internal working mechanism of a model, but also provides a certain basis for further optimizing and improving the model performance.

articleTitle: Global Context-Aware Framework for Accurate Lane Detection and Appearance Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: With the advancement of autonomous driving technology, lane detection has become a crucial component of autonomous systems. As part of road markings, it ensures vehicles stay within the correct lanes, reducing traffic accidents. This is particularly vital on highways and in complex urban environments, where challenges such as occlusions, reflections, shadows, and curves demand precise detection for safer decision-making. Lane appearance, defined by colors and solid or dashed styles, guides actions like lane changes and overtaking, making accurate recognition essential for dynamic path planning. To address these challenges, we propose an end-to-end network using hybrid anchors for joint detection of lane positions and appearances. Given the elongated shape of lane markings, the network enhances lateral features with horizontal convolution, employs attention mechanisms for global channel features. We use large kernels to expand receptive fields for existence prediction, and small kernels to refine position predictions, with a fully connected layer handling appearance classification. A novel loss function optimizes the network by leveraging the positional trends of adjacent lanes. Experiments on the TuSimple and LVLane datasets validate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in both detection and classification.

articleTitle: Multi-agent Simulation of Complex Economic Systems Driven by Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: In economics, the study of macroeconomic laws often encounters challenges such as difficulties in data collection and low data quality. A complex economic system (CES) simulation model based on Multi-agent Simulation (MAS) was designed and proposed to provide reliable, high-quality virtual data support for economic research to address these issues. To enhance the intelligence of agent behaviors in the simulation model, an economic agent decision-making model based on the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm was developed, and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the TD3 algorithm in CES simulations. Additionally, the model's decision-making capability in complex economic environments was further improved by incorporating Long Short-term Memory (LSTM) networks to handle temporal relationships. The research presented herein explores the application effects of deep reinforcement learning in economic research, providing a reliable source of virtual economic data for theoretical economic research and offering new perspectives and methods for economic system simulation research.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Relation Extraction Method Based on Data Augmentation with Large Language Models and Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Few-shot relation extraction is a subtask of relation extraction, aiming to identify new relations by learning from a small number of labeled instances. Most existing few-shot relation extraction methods mainly rely on fine-tuning techniques of pre-trained language models combined with traditional data augmentation methods, which fail to effectively address the issue of insufficient instances, leading to difficulties in improving the performance of few-shot relation classification tasks. Inspired by the latest advances in large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, we propose a few-shot relation extraction method based on data augmentation with large language models and contrastive learning (CLDA-FSRE). This method utilizes large pre-trained models for data augmentation and employs prompt-based learning to guide the large language models, enabling the model to exhibit strong domain adaptation capabilities even in scenarios with limited data. To further mitigate the overfitting problem under few-shot conditions, we introduce a contrastive learning module and a dynamic task weighting mechanism to focus on the learning of difficult tasks. Our experimental results are generally consistent with our design expectations, demonstrating the effectiveness of this method on the FewRel 1.0 and FewRel 2.0 datasets.

articleTitle: PIKGMA: PrIori Knowledge-Guided Multimodal Alignment And Domain Adaptation For Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: Multimodal domain adaptive emotion recognition aims to utilize the feature information of multiple modalities to achieve cross-domain emotion recognition, and how to constrain the inconsistency between inner-domain and cross-domain modality properly has been a hot spot in research. To address the above challenges, we propose a priori knowledge-guided multimodal alignment domain adaptive emotion recognition model, PIKGMA. PIKGMA is a semi-supervised multimodal physiological signal domain adaptation model for emotion recognition. It aligns multimodal emotion features draw support from inner-domain modalities alignment and cross-domain modalities alignment. Meanwhile, to better utilize the priori knowledge from the source domain (the data distribution of the source domain), we propose the priori dual-alignment bank strategy. The memory bank can be used to assist in cross-domain modality alignment and pseudo-label generation for domain adaptation. We conducted detailed experiments using two physiological signals on the DREAMER dataset, and the experimental results show that PIKGMA performs very well and is superior to existing methods.

articleTitle: Utilizing Ensemble Machine Learning for Improved Sentiment Analysis of Student Comments on Teaching Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: This work describes an ensemble machine learning approach to improve sentiment analysis of student comments about teaching performance. While traditional assessment tools, such as numerical ratings, provide limited insights, open-ended feedback provides richer qualitative data that reflects students' perspectives. However, manual analysis of such data could be more efficient and consistent. This work develops a robust stacking ensemble model employing Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression, and Random Forest as base classifiers and Logistic Regression as meta-classifiers. The ensemble approach takes advantage of the capabilities of individual classifiers to improve accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores in positive, neutral, and negative sentiment classes. 3,312 student comments were prepared using TF-IDF feature extraction, tokenization, and transformation, among other data preparation techniques. GridSearchCV was used to tune hyperparameters, and the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) was used to manage the class imbalance. With an overall accuracy of 0.87, the ensemble model exceeded individual models, particularly with underrepresented negative emotions. Importantly, it demonstrated balanced performance across all sentiment categories, reassuring the model's reliability. This study demonstrates the efficiency of ensemble learning in educational sentiment analysis, giving valuable insights for data-driven teaching quality improvements. Future work includes incorporating deep learning models like RNNs and transformers to improve performance even more and advanced vectorization techniques like Word2Vec and GloVe.

articleTitle: Personalized Recommendation Algorithm Based on Graph Embedding and Temporal Context Representation Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning technology and the wide application of intelligent recommendation systems, how to apply deep learning technology to intelligent recommendation systems to continuously improve the recommendation effect has always been a hot research direction. User historical behavior information plays an increasingly important role in the evolution and iteration of the recommender system model. Focusing on how to make full use of the time context of user behavior, how to better deal with the sparsity of massive data and system cold-start problem, the personalized recommendation algorithm is proposed. This algorithm represents the time sequence behavior data with the graph network structure, uses the graph representation learning model node2vec to obtain the graph embedding representation of users and items in the hyperparameter space, and introduces IF_ISF for the negative sampling to improve the model efficiency, and then generates the embedding representation of the user temporal context by the sum-pooling method, and also generates the embedding representation of the static attribute information of users and items by the deep semantic matching method based on DSSM, and finally concatenates the feature vector and uses the machine learning model XGBoost for recommendation ranking prediction. The ablation experiments through the comparison of multiple models on the MovieLens_1M public dataset show that the proposed algorithm is better than the baseline algorithm on the three indicators of MAE, Macro_F1 and Micro_F1, which has different degrees of improvement and can effectively improve the recommendation accuracy and satisfaction.

articleTitle: Compress YOLOv5 via Convolution Filters Reconstruction for the Application in Smart City Governance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE 17th International Conference on Computer Research and Development (ICCRD)
abstract: In the realm of smart city governance, object detection techniques have become increasingly integral. With the YOLO architecture emerges, it has become a prominent choice for detection due to its efficiency and accuracy. Despite such advantages, the computational demands of YOLO pose challenges for deployment on platforms with limited resources in many real applications. To address this, we introduce an compression methodology tailored for the YOLO model, aiming at enhancing the operational efficiency and practical applicability within the context of urban management. Specifically, for a convolutional layer, we reconstruct the convolution filters based on a set of filter bases, whose amount is much lower than original number of convolution filters. Using YOLOv5 as a case study, we implement the method by replacing the convolutional layer in C3 modules with our proposed new filters. The empirical evaluation of our method, conducted on three custom datasets, demonstrates that the compressed YOLOv5 model attains a substantial reduction in both parameter and FLOPs count, while maintaining the detection accuracy. This verifies the effectiveness of proposed method in practical applications. In addition, we also explore the specific impact of different compression strategies and parameter setting on model performance. The findings offer valuable insights into optimizing the balance between model scale and detection accuracy, contributing to the development of efficient object detection solution for resource constrained devices in smart city governance.
